answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when it is caught coordinating fraud, while limiting each account’s influence until it has completed costly, independently verified work. A knoll of fresh accounts cannot gain trust merely by appearing; each must lock capital and earn a track record. Like an ember spreading through a canyon, copied behavior can still expose a coordinated cluster, but the attacker risks losing stakes across every linked identity and must repeat the work for each one.
